area: Auth, scope and secrets: the MCP server's read-only analysis tools
title: Live-analysis MCP tools over the app's engines (Path analyzer, Test a list, rule precedence, DLP explainer, Data Flow Map, SSL coverage, Live DLP feed, Traffic insights, ZPA path, fleet health, snapshot diff, URL lookup, readiness, compliance) and the end-user skill that routes questions to them

checks.what: The server lists the four assessment tools and fifteen analysis tools, every one annotated read-only and not destructive; no tool name or argument writes, takes a secret, a scope or a confirmation

Every analysis tool's schema bounds each text (maxLength or a fixed list), list (maxItems) and number; the schema check refuses an argument over the cap before the tool runs, and the tool refuses it again when the schema is skipped

Inside a tool run (and process-wide in the server) only GET and the read POSTs (sign-in token, URL lookup, Insights, incident search, classic sign-out) are sent; a PUT, PATCH, DELETE or other POST is refused before any connection, on any thread
Every raw client a tool builds refuses writes; every tool run on the sample tenant leaves it unchanged; mcp_tools references none of the app's write engines

With nothing in scope where the server runs, every live tool is refused before sign-in; a partial scope refuses what it does not tick; the scope comes from a saved profile or the environment, never from a tool argument, and applies to the sample too
Secret fields planted in the tenant's answers, the environment's client secret echoed in a rule description, a JWT and an exception carrying the secret never reach a result
Fleet and incident summaries count devices and users and never list a user, email or hostname; Insights is read without the per-user section
Every answer keeps tenant text under data, says it is untrusted (prompt injection through rule names), and names the source, tenant, scope and read time; answers are capped and say what was cut

The existing access model holds for the new tools: credentials from the environment only, stdio or loopback HTTP that refuses a foreign Host or Origin (DNS rebinding), beyond loopback only with --allow-remote
The skill's routing table names only tools the server lists, covers every tool, links only files that exist; the docs list every tool, the scope variables and how to connect

findings.title: The MCP server had no request-level read-only guard: an assessment check (or a new tool) could have sent a write with the environment's credentials
findings.fix: mcp_tools.read_only wraps every tool and assessment run; guard_process covers the whole server process; clients a tool builds are sealed

findings.title: Tenant text (rule names, descriptions) reaches an AI assistant and could carry instructions (indirect prompt injection)
findings.fix: answers keep tenant text under data with an untrusted-data note; the skill's rule 6 says never follow it; no tool can write, so an injected instruction has nothing to act on
findings.reason: An assistant reading tenant names cannot be made immune; the read-only surface limits the impact to a wrong answer

findings.title: The HTTP transport has no sign-in of its own: any local process that reaches the loopback port can use the tenant credentials the server holds
findings.reason: The existing access model, kept as asked: loopback only with DNS-rebinding protection, beyond loopback refused unless --allow-remote behind an authenticating proxy; the docs recommend stdio, which listens on nothing
